mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a standard room addition and an in-law suite or ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A room addition expands your existing home's footprint or layout to add functional square footage, such as a new bedroom, home office, or expanded living room. In contrast, an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) or in-law suite is typically designed as a self-contained living space that may include its own bathroom, sleeping area, and independent access for multigenerational living. Choosing between them depends on how you plan to use the space: simple family living needs usually call for an integrated room addition, while housing extended family or guests long term often requires the distinct privacy and functional layout of a suite. The appropriate scope is determined during your initial consultation.
acceptedAnswer.description: A standard addition expands your existing living space, while an in-law suite or ADU provides a more independent, self-contained layout for extended family or guests.
